dnd-combat.name: dnd-combat
dnd-combat.description: Headless D&D 5e encounter authority: the SOLE writer of units + combatTiles + turn state (combatTiles is its own passability copy of the payload tiles, so composed dungeon-gen stays the sole writer of the rendered tiles). ENCOUNTER_START seeds units + tiles from its payload (the dungeon board builds them from dungeon-gen's FLOOR_GENERATED data; an empty tiles payload auto-generates an all-passable grid). Runs initiative via the dice atom (one ROLL per hop), player MOVE/ATTACK/END_TURN intents with strict SRD attack math (nat 20 crit doubles damage dice, nat 1 always misses), and a greedy manhattan melee monster AI processed one monster per internal MONSTER_STEP hop. Death saves are organic: when the hero unit starts a turn at 0 hp, combat rolls the save itself (purpose "deathsave" → DEATH_SAVE), honors HERO_REVIVED (unit back to 1 hp) / HERO_STABLE (unit marked stable, future turns skip the save), passes HERO_DAMAGE through with the crit flag, and bars a 0-hp hero from MOVE/ATTACK. Renders nothing.

dnd-dice.name: dnd-dice
dnd-dice.description: Headless D&D 5e dice authority: the SOLE writer of lastRoll + rollLog. Applies ROLL intents with structured {count,sides,bonus} specs (normal/advantage/disadvantage on a single d20), honors the deterministic rollQueue test hook (queue head per die, math/random fallback when it empties), and emits DICE_ROLLED. Renders nothing.

dnd-dungeon-gen.name: dnd-dungeon-gen
dnd-dungeon-gen.description: Headless D&D 5e dungeon-floor authority: the SOLE writer of tiles, features, monsterSpawns, floor, heroSpawn. GENERATE_FLOOR carves 5-7 non-overlapping rooms joined by L-corridors (connectivity guaranteed by construction, verified by flood-fill with a deterministic single-room fallback), places stairs-down in the last room, heroSpawn in the first, and depth-scaled monster/chest/trap markers. Renders nothing.

dnd-hero.name: dnd-hero
dnd-hero.description: Headless D&D 5e hero-sheet authority: the SOLE writer of the hero sheet (abilities, level, xp, proficiency, hp, maxHp, ac, conditions, deathSaves, status). Applies HERO_DAMAGE/HERO_HEAL/HERO_GAIN_XP/DEATH_SAVE intents with strict SRD math — damage while down/stable counts as death-save failures (1 per hit, 2 on a crit) and a stable hero resumes dying — and emits HERO_DOWN/HERO_DIED/HERO_LEVELED/HERO_REVIVED/HERO_STABLE. Traps are organic: TRAP_SPRUNG rolls a dex save through the dice atom (purpose save:dex:trap, config trapDc), a failure rolls config trapDamage (purpose trap:damage) and routes it through the hero's own HERO_DAMAGE path so the down/stable/death rules apply, and TRAP_SAVE reports the outcome. RESTART re-initializes the sheet from config for a fresh delve. Renders nothing.

dnd-narrator.name: dnd-narrator
dnd-narrator.description: Headless D&D 5e narrator: the SOLE writer of narration (the story feed), unitKinds (unit id → kind mirror), and quest. Listens to the whole delve bus — delve start, floor carved, turns, attacks, slays, death saves, traps, loot, level-ups, defeat — and prepends deterministic narration entries { id, title, status } composed from payloads (status ∈ pending=story | active=hero turn | error=foe/grim | complete=loot — the std timeline pattern's status vocabulary, so a `timeline` node renders the feed with tone-coded dots). ENCOUNTER_START mirrors id → kind into its own field so attack lines can name combatants without cross-trait entity reads. Renders nothing.

dnd-dungeon-board.name: dnd-dungeon-board

START_DELVE carves a floor; FLOOR_GENERATED builds combat's ENCOUNTER_START payload (hero from config heroStats at heroSpawn, monsters from monsterSpawns through the monsterStats roster) and mirrors features into its own knownFeatures (server runtimes scope entity reads per-trait); click a monster to ATTACK, a reachable tile to MOVE, D/Space/G or the sidebar buttons for DASH/END_TURN/DODGE. Stepping on a chest rolls 2d4+2 healing (purpose loot → HERO_HEAL + CHEST_LOOT), stepping on a trap fires TRAP_SPRUNG (hero sheet rolls the dex save); each feature fires once per floor (openedFeatures). Descending the stairs on a won floor regenerates deeper — unless it was config.finalFloor, which wins the run (result escaped + ESCAPED for the epilogue). The sidebar chronicles the narrator feed (tone → typography color), the last dice roll, the quest hook, and the action buttons.

dnd-dungeon-delver.name: dnd-dungeon-delver

Direct molecule-trait rebinding was the intended composition but is unsupported end-to-end: the compiler bars rebinding the board's interaction trait (fixed entity binding, ORB_T_ENTITY_NOT_REBINDABLE) and the JS runtime preprocessor only sees authored traits in an imported orbital, so an organism-level ref to a molecule's rebind trait (Board.traits.BoardDice) does not resolve — both recorded as gaps. BoardHero stays the sole writer of the hero sheet; the std game-hud only reads (the hud molecule's own hero rebind is NOT recomposed — that is the double-hero trap). Boot shows a start menu; START drives START_DELVE; chests/traps fire on the hero's step (loot 2d4+2 healing / dex-save trap damage), Dash (D) and Dodge (G) spend the action for movement or defense, the sidebar chronicles every event through the narrator atom with tone-colored lines; descending floor 3's stairs wins the run (YOU ESCAPED epilogue), hero death shows YOU DIED with Delve Again (RESTART + fresh START_DELVE).
dnd-dungeon-delver.capabilities: dnd dungeon delver, 5e dungeon crawler, tactical combat game, floor delve, start menu, defeat overlay, character hud, narrator story feed, dice chronicle, dash dodge actions, traps and chests, quest and epilogue

std-brick-breaker.name: std-brick-breaker
std-brick-breaker.description: Headless breakout mechanic: the SOLE writer of ball + px + bricks + score + lives + result. A tick advances the ball one cell; walls and the paddle bounce it, bricks shatter on contact (score +1, BURST particle), a ball past the paddle costs a life and re-serves, zero lives loses the run, clearing every brick wins it. Applies clamped PADDLE_SET intents and RESTART. Renders nothing.

std-evade-chase.name: std-evade-chase

Applies EVADE_MOVE intents (steps the hero one cell, clamped to the grid); a 1s tick steps three corner chasers one manhattan-sign cell toward the hero (blocked by the hero cell and each other's cells), adjacency deals 1 damage (hero 3 HP), each survived tick is the score, surviving surviveTicks ticks wins, and dropping to 0 HP loses. Applies RESTART. Renders nothing.

std-gravity-flap.name: std-gravity-flap
std-gravity-flap.description: Headless gravity-flap mechanic: the SOLE writer of birdY + vel + pipes + tickCount + score + result. A tick applies gravity to the bird, scrolls pipes left, spawns a new pipe every 8 ticks, scores each pipe that crosses the bird column, and sets result to lost on floor or pipe collision. Applies FLAP intents (upward impulse) and RESTART. Emits a BURST pickup particle on each score. Renders nothing.

std-lane-hazard.name: std-lane-hazard
std-lane-hazard.description: Headless lane-hazard mechanic: the SOLE writer of hazards + lives + result (plus its own tracked hero cell). A tick slides every hazard one cell along its lane (even lanes drift left, odd lanes drift right, wrapping at the edges); when a moved hazard shares the tracked hero cell, lives drop by one, HERO_HIT is emitted so the glue can send the hero home, and at zero lives the run is lost. Tracks the hero cell from HERO_STEPPED, listens PROGRESS — when no objectives remain the run is won — and RESTART to re-seed. Renders nothing.

std-pong-rally.name: std-pong-rally
std-pong-rally.description: Headless pong-rally mechanic: the SOLE writer of ball + leftY + rightY + leftScore + rightScore + result. A tick advances the ball by its velocity, bounces it off the top/bottom walls and both paddles (emitting a BURST particle on each paddle hit), and awards a point when a paddle misses — first to 5 sets result to left/right and emits GAME_END. When aiEnabled (default) the same tick steers the RIGHT paddle toward the ball for a single-player game vs AI; set aiEnabled false for two-player, where RIGHT_UP/RIGHT_DOWN move the right paddle by hand. Applies PADDLE_MOVE intents (side + dy, clamped to the playfield) and RESTART. Renders nothing.

std-snake-loop.name: std-snake-loop
std-snake-loop.description: Headless snake-loop mechanic: the SOLE writer of body + dir + food + score + result. A tick advances the head in @entity.dir; walls and self-collisions set result to lost; eating food grows the body, awards a point, respawns food on a provably free cell, and emits a BURST pickup particle. Applies TURN intents (180-degree reversals rejected) and RESTART. Renders nothing.

std-algo-selectionsort.description: Algorithm-animation engine (algorithm-canvas): Selection-sort visualizer — each step performs one scan-compare or one settle-swap micro-step over a bar array, with pointers on the fill position, the running minimum and the scan cursor, a fill range over the sorted prefix and a bracket range over the active scan span. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (SelectionSortTransport); the scan-compare/settle-swap logic lives in the sibling SelectionSortSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (applies one scan-compare or settle-swap micro-step), LEARN_RESET (reseeds bars from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.SelectionSortTransport — one render authority per shared entity). Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-algo-slidingwindow.name: std-algo-slidingwindow
std-algo-slidingwindow.description: Sliding-window (max sum) visualizer — an algorithm-canvas bar array with l/r pointers, a blue fill range over the live window and a green fill range over the best window found so far; each step slides the fixed-size window right one position. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (SlidingWindowTransport); the window slide lives in the sibling SlidingWindowSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (slides the window right and tracks the best sum), LEARN_RESET (reseeds bars/pointers/ranges from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.SlidingWindowTransport — one render authority per shared entity). Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-algo-stack.name: std-algo-stack
std-algo-stack.description: Stack engine — bounded vertical slot array on algorithm-canvas: Push writes the next value at the top cursor and the stack grows upward from slot 0 at the bottom, Pop clears the top slot (LIFO), and a top pointer tracks the last pushed slot in the pointer band; a few slots are pre-seeded so the first paint already shows a stack. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-algo-toposort.name: std-algo-toposort
std-algo-toposort.description: Topological sort visualizer (Kahn) — an algo-graph-canvas (layered layout, directed edges) badges every node with its live in-degree; nodes at in-degree 0 turn frontier (ready), the node each step emits turns current, then visited, while every successor's badge drops by one. A horizontal strip below the graph (algorithm-canvas slots) fills left-to-right with the emitted order as it grows. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (ToposortTransport); the Kahn expansion lives in the sibling ToposortSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (applies one in-degree-0 emit and relaxation), LEARN_RESET (reseeds the whole DAG), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.ToposortTransport — one render authority per shared entity). Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-algo-twopointer.name: std-algo-twopointer
std-algo-twopointer.description: Two-sum (two-pointer) visualizer — an algorithm-canvas bar array with left/right pointers and a fill range spanning the active window; each step compares the pair sum against the target and moves the pointer that needs to change. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (TwoPointerTransport); the two-pointer scan lives in the sibling TwoPointerSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (applies one compare-and-move), LEARN_RESET (reseeds the array and pointers), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.TwoPointerTransport — one render authority per shared entity). Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-astro-orbit-3d.name: std-astro-orbit-3d
std-astro-orbit-3d.description: 3D solar-system orbital instrument — integrates a config-declared planet roster about a fixed emissive Sun under softened inverse-square gravity in scene cells every tick, demonstrating real solar-system geometry a 2D canvas cannot show: the inner planets on near-circular coplanar orbits, Pluto's 17° inclination tilted off the ecliptic, and Halley's comet on a highly eccentric perihelion slingshot — with named planet/period readouts and named Kepler presets stepped through in place, rendered on a 3D physics-canvas; composed as the orbit-3d mode of the learning astronomy lab. The Run/Pause/Reset/speed transport and the sim clock come from the std-learn-sim-3d atom (AstroOrbit3DSim); the gravity physics and preset roster live in the sibling AstroOrbit3DPhysics trait, which transitions directly on the transport's SIM_3D_TICK (integrates the bodies from ?dt) and SIM_3D_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport shell is embedded via @trait.AstroOrbit3DSim — one render authority per shared entity). Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-astro-orbit.name: std-astro-orbit
std-astro-orbit.description: Kepler orbit simulator — the learner drags eccentricity and semi-major-axis sliders while the planet steps along its ellipse, watching equal-area sweeps confirm Kepler's second law, on a math-canvas authored entirely in world coordinates. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (AstroOrbitTransport); the equal-area stepping lives in the sibling AstroOrbitSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (advances the planet by one equal-time, equal-area interval), LEARN_RESET (returns the planet to perihelion without changing eccentricity or axis), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.AstroOrbitTransport — one render authority per shared entity); dragging the eccentricity or semi-major-axis sliders remains its own domain affordance and reseeds the orbit immediately. The orbit never terminates — done stays false throughout. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-astro-stellar.name: std-astro-stellar
std-astro-stellar.description: Stellar life-cycle simulator — the learner picks a starting mass via slider or preset buttons and steps through the star's evolutionary stages from nebula to its predicted end state (white dwarf, neutron star, or black hole), on a math-canvas with a poor-man's stage-progress timeline. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (AstroStellarTransport); the stage-advance lives in the sibling AstroStellarSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (advances the star to its next life-cycle stage — the same computation the tick used to run, and the same as the old Next Stage button), LEARN_RESET (returns the star to its first life-cycle stage), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.AstroStellarTransport — one render authority per shared entity). The life-cycle path terminates: done flips true once the star reaches its path's final stage (white dwarf / neutron star / black hole), halting the transport's clock and blocking further LEARN_STEP transitions until Reset. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-bio-cell-3d.name: std-bio-cell-3d
std-bio-cell-3d.description: 3D eukaryotic-cell ultrastructure explorer — a config-declared organelle roster (nucleus, nucleolus, mitochondria, rough/smooth ER, Golgi, ribosomes, lysosome, centrioles, peroxisome) rendered as an orbit-rotatable volumetric scene with cytoskeleton-hint edges; clicking an organelle or pressing Tour retargets the camera onto it, enlarges it, and narrates its function, with a progress readout tracking the tour and the membrane toured as the enclosing boundary. Composed as a domain binding of the std-learn-tour-3d guided-tour atom — the organelle roster and cytoskeleton edges are config overrides on its station/edge knobs. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-bio-cell.name: std-bio-cell
std-bio-cell.description: Eukaryotic cell-structure lab — a config-declared organelle roster the learner tours with Prev/Next; the selected organelle highlights and its function is narrated, and a progress readout tracks the tour. A plantMode knob adds chloroplast, cell wall, and central vacuole. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (BioCellTransport); the tour-advance logic lives in the sibling BioCellSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (advances to the next organelle — the same computation the tick used to run, and the same as Next), LEARN_RESET (reseeds the tour to the first organelle, clearing visited history and tour-complete), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.BioCellTransport — one render authority per shared entity); Prev and Next remain as their own domain buttons for manual bidirectional stepping. The tour cycles indefinitely, wrapping past the last organelle back to the first — done stays false always, there is no rest/completion condition to detect; tourComplete is a separate domain flag marking when every organelle has been visited at least once, but stepping continues past that point. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-bio-dna-3d.name: std-bio-dna-3d
std-bio-dna-3d.description: 3D DNA double-helix explorer — a config-declared helix (base-pair count, rise per base pair, twist per base pair, radius) procedurally wound by the biology-canvas helix3d substrate into two antiparallel sugar-phosphate backbones with A-T / G-C rungs colored by base; Tour steps through didactic stations (overall helix, one base pair, backbone, major and minor grooves) retargeting the camera with a caption, clicking a rung names the pair and its hydrogen-bond count (A=T two, G≡C three), and Unwind separates the first base pairs as a replication-fork hint. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (DNA3DTransport); the tour-advance logic lives in the sibling DNA3DSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (advances to the next station — the same computation the tick used to run, and the same as Tour), LEARN_RESET (reseeds the tour to the first station, clearing visited history, tour-complete, and the unwound/selected-pair state), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.DNA3DTransport — one render authority per shared entity); Tour remains as its own domain button for manual advance (identical computation to the transport's Step), and Unwind and base-pair click selection remain their own domain affordances. The tour cycles indefinitely, wrapping past the last station back to the first — done stays false always, there is no rest/completion condition to detect; tourComplete is a separate domain flag marking when every station has been visited at least once, but stepping continues past that point. Composed of a biology-canvas in 3D mode plus the transport atom. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-bio-dna-replication.name: std-bio-dna-replication
std-bio-dna-replication.description: DNA replication engine — a biology-canvas helix ladder built from a config sequence knob; each step advances the replication fork one base pair, marking rungs behind the fork as newly synthesized, the frontier rung as open, and rungs ahead as still paired, narrating the base pair at the fork. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (DNAReplicationTransport); the fork-advance logic lives in the sibling DNAReplicationSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (advances the fork one base pair — the same computation the tick used to run), LEARN_RESET (reseeds the helix from the configured sequence, resetting the fork to base 0), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.DNAReplicationTransport — one render authority per shared entity). The stage sequence terminates: once the fork reaches the last base pair, DNAReplicationSim sets done true (its sole writer) and the transport clock halts — LEARN_STEP is guarded on not done. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches. Composed by learning-biology-lab as mode dna-replication.

std-bio-foodweb.name: std-bio-foodweb
std-bio-foodweb.description: Trophic-dynamics simulator — a config-declared species roster and feeding-edge graph; each generation producers regrow toward capacity while consumers gain from what they eat and lose to predation and decay, node radii and count labels tracking population across a directed feeding-edge biology-canvas with per-species population traces, and narration explains what changed. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (BioFoodwebTransport); the trophic-cascade computation lives in the sibling BioFoodwebSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (advances one generation of growth/predation/decay across the roster), LEARN_RESET (reseeds the species roster, traces, and narration from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.BioFoodwebTransport — one render authority per shared entity); Remove target and Boost target remain as their own domain buttons to perturb the config-designated species and trigger a cascade. The trophic dynamics never terminate — done stays false always, there is no rest/completion condition to detect. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-bio-mitosis.name: std-bio-mitosis
std-bio-mitosis.description: Cell-division engine — a config-declared five-phase roster (interphase→prophase→metaphase→anaphase→telophase) the learner steps through on biology-canvas: a timeline strip tracks phase progress, the cell boundary renders as a compartment, chromosome nodes reposition per the phase's declarative scene roster, and a cleavage furrow compartment appears at telophase. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (BioMitosisTransport); the phase advance lives in the sibling BioMitosisSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (advances one phase), LEARN_RESET (reseeds from the first phase), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.BioMitosisTransport — one render authority per shared entity). Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-bio-network.name: std-bio-network
std-bio-network.description: Generic declarative biology-network renderer — a fixed roster of nodes/edges/shapes (cells and organelles, food-web trophic links, or classification taxa) drawn on a biology-canvas; each step advances a highlight cursor through the node roster, narrating the current node's label while adjacent nodes stay default and everything else mutes. Node/edge/shape vocabulary is entirely config-declared, so the same mechanism serves any static biology diagram. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (BioNetworkTransport); the cursor advance lives in the sibling BioNetworkSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (advances the cursor to the next node, wrapping back to the start — this diagram has no completion state, so done stays false), LEARN_RESET (reseeds the cursor and node states from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.BioNetworkTransport — one render authority per shared entity). Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-bio-phasecycle.name: std-bio-phasecycle
std-bio-phasecycle.description: Staged biology phase-cycle engine — the learner steps a Next/Prev cursor through an ordered roster of stages (e.g. mitosis phases), each revealing its own node/edge/shape snapshot, label, and description, and can predict the next stage before revealing it for immediate correct/incorrect feedback. A ring overview tracks done/active/pending progress through the roster. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (BioPhaseCycleTransport); the phase-cycle stepping lives in the sibling BioPhaseCycleSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (advances to the next phase), LEARN_RESET (reseeds from phase 0), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.BioPhaseCycleTransport — one render authority per shared entity). Stage vocabulary is entirely config-declared, so the same mechanism serves any staged biology process, on a biology-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-bio-population.name: std-bio-population
std-bio-population.description: Predator-prey population engine — real coupled Lotka-Volterra dynamics: each Step integrates one dt of prey growth-vs-predation and predator growth-vs-death, redrawing two organism nodes (radius proportional to population) linked by a directed "eats" edge on biology-canvas, with a two-series traces panel tracking prey/predator history. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (BioPopulationTransport); the Lotka-Volterra integration lives in the sibling BioPopulationSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (integrates one dt of the coupled predator-prey dynamics), LEARN_RESET (reseeds populations, history, scene nodes, and narration from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.BioPopulationTransport — one render authority per shared entity). The predator-prey dynamics never terminate — done stays false always, there is no rest/completion condition to detect. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-bio-processrate.name: std-bio-processrate
std-bio-processrate.description: Photosynthesis-style process-rate engine — the learner adjusts light, CO₂, and temperature sliders and watches the process rate and its limiting factor recompute live, with input-node radii/colors on a biology-canvas reflecting each factor's saturation. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (BioProcessRateTransport); the environmental-scenario cycling lives in the sibling BioProcessRateSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (advances to the next config-declared scenario — low light, high CO₂, high temperature, balanced — applying all three inputs at once), LEARN_RESET (restores the config-declared starting light/CO₂/temperature and scenario index), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.BioProcessRateTransport — one render authority per shared entity); the light/CO₂/temperature sliders remain their own domain affordances for direct manual adjustment between scenario steps. Scenario cycling never terminates — done stays false always, there is no rest/completion condition to detect. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-branching-logic.name: std-branching-logic
std-branching-logic.description: std-branching-logic — survey skip-logic rules. Lists rules in `browsing`; opens rule detail in `viewing_single` with Edit / Delete actions.

std-chem-crystal-3d.name: std-chem-crystal-3d
std-chem-crystal-3d.description: 3D crystal-lattice instrument — a config-declared roster of lattices (simple cubic, body-centered cubic, face-centered cubic, rock-salt NaCl, diamond) rendered by the chemistry-canvas lattice3d substrate into 2×2×2 unit-cell blocks the learner steps through with Prev/Next (clamped at the roster ends) or auto-run (wraps past the last lattice back to the first), each an orbit-rotatable ball-and-stick scene, with a unit-cell highlight toggle (unit-cell atoms full color, the rest dimmed via color) and a caption naming coordination number, atoms per unit cell, and packing efficiency. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (ChemCrystal3DTransport); the lattice-advance logic lives in the sibling ChemCrystal3DSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (advances to the next lattice, wrapping past the last back to the first — the same wrapping computation the old auto-advance tick ran), LEARN_RESET (reseeds the roster to the first lattice, clearing the unit-cell highlight and atom selection), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.ChemCrystal3DTransport — one render authority per shared entity); Prev, Next, the unit-cell toggle, and atom selection remain as their own domain arms. The clock wraps indefinitely — done stays false always, matching the old tick's behavior, which never set a completion flag at the roster boundary. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-chem-diffusion.name: std-chem-diffusion
std-chem-diffusion.description: Diffusion engine — two color-coded gases random-walk across a shared box; each Step applies substeps of the walk, and honest narration only claims mixing when the left/right species imbalance actually shrank that step. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (ChemDiffusionTransport); the random-walk diffusion lives in the sibling ChemDiffusionSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (applies one substepped random-walk pass), LEARN_RESET (reseeds particles, containers, readouts, and narration from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.ChemDiffusionTransport — one render authority per shared entity). Diffusion never terminates — done stays false always, there is no rest/completion condition to detect. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-chem-molecule-3d.name: std-chem-molecule-3d
std-chem-molecule-3d.description: 3D molecular-geometry (VSEPR) instrument — a config-declared roster of molecules (water, ammonia, methane, carbon dioxide, boron trifluoride) the learner steps through with Prev/Next (clamped at the roster ends) or the transport clock (wraps past the last molecule back to the first), each rendered as an orbit-rotatable ball-and-stick scene on a 3D chemistry-canvas, with a details toggle revealing the geometry/bond-angle readout and click-to-select atom highlighting with a caption. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (ChemMolecule3DTransport); the roster-advance logic lives in the sibling ChemMolecule3DSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (advances to the next molecule, wrapping — the same computation the old auto-advance tick ran), LEARN_RESET (reseeds the roster to the first molecule, clearing details/selection), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.ChemMolecule3DTransport — one render authority per shared entity); Prev, Next, and Details remain as their own domain buttons for manual bidirectional stepping and readout toggling. Prev/Next clamp at the roster ends (unchanged domain behavior) while the transport clock wraps (cloned from the old tick) — done stays false always, there is no rest/completion condition to detect. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-chem-molecule.name: std-chem-molecule
std-chem-molecule.description: Molecule gallery — a config-declared roster of real molecules (water, methane, ammonia, carbon dioxide) the learner steps through with Next Molecule, each rendered from fractional atom positions with its own lone pairs, partial charges, bond orders, formula and geometry caption. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (ChemMoleculeTransport); the roster-advance logic lives in the sibling ChemMoleculeSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (advances to the next molecule — the same computation the tick used to run, and the same as Next Molecule), LEARN_RESET (reseeds the roster to startPresetIndex), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.ChemMoleculeTransport — one render authority per shared entity); Next Molecule remains as its own domain button for manual stepping. The roster cycles indefinitely, wrapping past the last preset back to the first — done stays false always, there is no rest/completion condition to detect. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-chem-osmosis.name: std-chem-osmosis
std-chem-osmosis.description: Osmosis engine — water random-walks freely across a dashed semipermeable membrane while confined solute stays on its side, biasing water toward the solute side to equalize concentration; each Step applies substeps of the walk and counts the actual net water crossings that step. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (ChemOsmosisTransport); the random-walk lives in the sibling ChemOsmosisSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (applies one substepped walk pass and counts net crossings), LEARN_RESET (reseeds particles, containers, and readouts from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.ChemOsmosisTransport — one render authority per shared entity). Osmosis never reaches equilibrium in this model — the random walk runs indefinitely, so done stays false-only and the transport clock never halts on its own. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-chem-reaction-3d.name: std-chem-reaction-3d
std-chem-reaction-3d.description: 3D reaction-mechanism instrument — a config-declared multi-stage mechanism (default: SN2 nucleophilic substitution, Nu⁻ + CH₃-Br → [Nu···C···Br]‡ → Nu-CH₃ + Br⁻) the learner steps through with Prev/Next or the transport clock, each stage rendered as an orbit-rotatable ball-and-stick scene on a 3D chemistry-canvas with a per-stage caption (what breaks, what forms, why the geometry inverts — the Walden inversion only 3D can show, partial bonds at the transition state drawn pale). The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (ChemReaction3DTransport); the stage-advance logic lives in the sibling ChemReaction3DSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (advances to the next mechanism stage — the same computation the old auto-advance tick ran), LEARN_RESET (reseeds the mechanism to the first stage/reactants), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.ChemReaction3DTransport — one render authority per shared entity); Prev and Next remain as their own domain buttons for manual bidirectional stepping. The mechanism is finite: reaching the last stage sets done true (the sibling is done's sole writer), halting the transport clock — the same stop-at-the-end behavior the old auto-advance tick enforced by clearing running; Reset clears done and returns to the first stage (reactants). Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-chem-reaction.name: std-chem-reaction
std-chem-reaction.description: Reversible reaction engine — pairCount A+B pairs run one kinetic interval per Step: each dissociated pair draws against kf to form, each bonded pair draws against kr to break, and positions glide toward the bonded center or back to their home over substeps; bonds mark forming/breaking/highlight and narration claims equilibrium only when the bonded count doesn't net change. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (ChemReactionTransport); the reaction kinetics live in the sibling ChemReactionSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (applies one kf/kr draw-and-glide interval), LEARN_RESET (reseeds atoms, pairs, bonds, and readouts from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.ChemReactionTransport — one render authority per shared entity). Reaction never explicitly terminates in this atom — done stays false, there is no rest/completion condition currently wired. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-chem-titration.name: std-chem-titration
std-chem-titration.description: Acid-base titration engine — composed as a domain binding of the std-learn-doser generic dosing instrument: the learner adds titrant in large or small increments (or lets it auto-drip) through the doser's dosing/clock/band mechanism (ChemTitrationDoser), while a sibling trait (ChemTitrationSim) transitions directly on the doser's DOSE_ADDED/DOSE_RESET/DOSER_UPDATED broadcasts, computes the acid-base stoichiometry (pH from titrant volume, strong/weak Ka branching), and renders the beaker/burette/pH-vs-mL scene — the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use, one render authority per shared entity. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-civics-billprocess.name: std-civics-billprocess
std-civics-billprocess.description: How a bill becomes law — a bill token travels Introduced -> House vote -> Senate vote -> President, with veto and a two-thirds congressional override, on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-civics-checks.name: std-civics-checks
std-civics-checks.description: Checks-and-balances matrix — the learner names which branch of government can check a given governmental action, drawing the check arrow actor -> checker on a three-branch diagram, on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-civics-electoral.name: std-civics-electoral
std-civics-electoral.description: Electoral-college sandbox — flip swing states and watch Red/Blue electoral-vote totals race the 270 threshold, with a popular-vs-electoral split readout, on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-civics-gerrymander.name: std-civics-gerrymander
std-civics-gerrymander.description: Gerrymandering sandbox — assign precincts on a grid to districts, then evaluate seats won and the efficiency gap to see packing and cracking in action, on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-earth-plates-3d.name: std-earth-plates-3d
std-earth-plates-3d.description: 3D plate-tectonics cross-section explorer — a config-declared block-section through a convergent margin (oceanic slab bending down under continental crust, trench, Wadati-Benioff seismic zone, volcanic arc, mantle convection cell) rendered as an orbit-rotatable volumetric scene, with Next Boundary (STEP) cycling convergent/divergent/transform boundary presets and a Tour that retargets the camera onto each highlighted feature and narrates it — the subduction geometry a flat 2D section cannot rotate. Composes the std-learn-tour-3d guided-tour atom (EarthPlates3DSim) on ONE shared entity: the tour contract renders the scene — 4 narrated station highlights per preset riding on a `backdrop` of non-station block geometry — while the sibling Plates3DPresets trait owns only the preset fields and renders the full shell with the tour shell embedded (@trait.EarthPlates3DSim — one render authority per shared entity); STEP hot-swaps the roster through the tour atom's single-writer SYNC_STATIONS entry point, and every tour update repaints the full shell (the sibling transitions directly on the TOUR_3D_UPDATED broadcast — the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use). Reset restarts the tour within the active preset. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-earth-plates.name: std-earth-plates
std-earth-plates.description: Plate-tectonics boundary simulator — the learner picks a convergent/divergent/transform boundary and advances motion to see landforms and earthquakes accumulate, on a biology-canvas with crust/asthenosphere bands and directed motion edges. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (EarthPlatesTransport); the boundary-motion computation lives in the sibling EarthPlatesSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (advances plate motion by one step and recomputes landforms, earthquakes, and geometry — the same computation the tick used to run, and the same as the old Advance button), LEARN_RESET (reseeds boundary selection, advance progress, and motion geometry from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.EarthPlatesTransport — one render authority per shared entity); Select Boundary remains its own domain button to pick convergent/divergent/transform. The simulator terminates — advanceSteps caps at maxAdvanceSteps, at which point EarthPlatesSim (the sole writer of done) sets done true; LEARN_RESET clears it back to false. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-earth-watercycle.name: std-earth-watercycle
std-earth-watercycle.description: Water-cycle flux simulator — the learner drives solar input and steps the cycle to watch evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and runoff fluxes rebalance across ocean, atmosphere, and land reservoirs, on a biology-canvas with sky/land/ocean bands and directed flux edges. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (EarthWatercycleTransport); the flux computation lives in the sibling EarthWatercycleSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (drifts solar input by solarStepDelta and recomputes evaporation/condensation/precipitation/runoff fluxes — the same computation the tick used to run, and the same as the old Step the Cycle button), LEARN_RESET (reseeds solar input, cycle step, fluxes, and narration from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.EarthWatercycleTransport — one render authority per shared entity). The water cycle never terminates — done stays false always, there is no rest/completion condition to detect. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-econ-elasticity.name: std-econ-elasticity
std-econ-elasticity.description: Price-elasticity-of-demand engine — the learner moves a price along a configurable linear demand curve (and shifts the curve's intercept) while the instrument computes live point and arc elasticity, shades the total-revenue rectangle, and pronounces an elastic / inelastic / unit-elastic verdict, on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-econ-gdp.name: std-econ-gdp
std-econ-gdp.description: GDP expenditure-approach engine — the learner raises or lowers consumption, investment, government spending and net exports bars and GDP (= C + I + G + (X − M)) recomputes live on a math-canvas; an optional 'counts in GDP?' classify mini-game quizzes which transactions enter GDP. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-econ-market.name: std-econ-market
std-econ-market.description: Supply-and-demand market engine — the learner shifts demand/supply curve intercepts and sets a price to see surplus or shortage emerge against the computed equilibrium, on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-econ-monopoly.name: std-econ-monopoly
std-econ-monopoly.description: Monopoly pricing engine — demand, marginal-revenue, marginal-cost and average-total-cost curves on a math-canvas; the learner sets output with a slider and sees the profit box, the deadweight-loss triangle versus the competitive benchmark (toggleable), and the markup over marginal cost. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-econ-phillips.name: std-econ-phillips
std-econ-phillips.description: Phillips-curve engine — a demand shock moves the economy along the short-run Phillips curve (inflation π = expected inflation − slope × (unemployment − natural rate)); each adjustment step adaptively raises expectations and returns unemployment to the natural rate, so the long-run Phillips curve is vertical and the inflation–unemployment tradeoff collapses, on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-econ-ppf.name: std-econ-ppf
std-econ-ppf.description: Production-possibilities frontier engine — the learner drags an allocation slider dividing resources between two goods, reads the marginal opportunity cost, and toggles an idle-resources demo that drops actual output inside the frontier, on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-geo-dtm-3d.name: std-geo-dtm-3d
std-geo-dtm-3d.description: 3D digital terrain model — an 11×11 grid of terrain samples whose height (scene z) follows a config-selected terrain function (elongated sine ridgeline with a secondary frequency, an inverted valley/canyon, or a radial central peak inside a bowl), rendered as a continuous banded heightfield surface (surface3d) colored by an elevation ramp from deep water blue through green lowlands and brown highlands to white peaks, with clickable elevation-post bodies at every sample, a water-level knob that floods every band below the datum, and a click readout of each sample's elevation, slope estimate against its grid neighbors, and contour band — the relief geometry a 2D contour map can only hint at; composed as the dtm-3d mode of the learning geography lab. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-geo-dtm.name: std-geo-dtm
std-geo-dtm.description: Demographic transition model engine — stages 1-5 redraw piecewise birth/death rate curves on a math-canvas; the learner pages through stages and drives birth/death rate sliders to reproduce each stage's target rates within a tolerance. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-geo-koppen.name: std-geo-koppen
std-geo-koppen.description: Simplified Köppen climate classifier engine — the learner sets a summer/winter temperature and average-monthly-precipitation profile and a 12-month climograph classifies the climate by first-match-wins rule, on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-geo-population.name: std-geo-population
std-geo-population.description: Age-sex population pyramid engine — the learner drives birth/death/migration rate dials and steps a five-cohort cohort-component projection, reading the dependency ratio and pyramid shape classification on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-geo-urban.name: std-geo-urban
std-geo-urban.description: Urban land-use model engine — Burgess concentric, Hoyt sector, and Harris-Ullman multiple-nuclei overlays toggle on a config-declared city map; the learner cycles each zone's land-use tag and checks how many zones match the selected model's prediction, on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-geo-vonthunen.name: std-geo-vonthunen
std-geo-vonthunen.description: Von Thünen bid-rent engine — each crop draws a bid-rent line (rent versus distance to market) on a math-canvas; the transport-cost and market-price dials shift every line's slope and intercept, and the concentric ring boundaries (line intersections) redraw live. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-hist-causalchain.name: std-hist-causalchain
std-hist-causalchain.description: WWI causal-chain counterfactual engine — the learner toggles structural causes and triggers off/on, a dependency cascade removes any cause whose enabling edge is gone, and the summed contribution of active causes is compared against a war threshold on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-hist-ccot.name: std-hist-ccot
std-hist-ccot.description: CCOT (continuity and change over time) instrument — the learner moves a time cursor along an indicator curve, tags each era as continuity or a turning point, and checks the verdict against the canonical reading on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-hist-comparison.name: std-hist-comparison
std-hist-comparison.description: Comparison instrument — the learner attaches traits to two case columns and snaps traits true of both into the shared center, then checks the Venn-style verdict against the canonical shared traits on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-hist-periodization.name: std-hist-periodization
std-hist-periodization.description: Periodization instrument — the learner places events on a timeline and draws era boundaries, then checks the result against the canonical boundaries within a year tolerance on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-hist-sourcing.name: std-hist-sourcing
std-hist-sourcing.description: HIPP sourcing instrument — the learner classifies each aspect of a historical source (historical situation, intended audience, purpose, point of view, and primary vs secondary) from fixed option rows, scored live against the source's canonical attribution on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-ling-ipa.name: std-ling-ipa
std-ling-ipa.description: IPA consonant-chart explorer and quiz — the learner selects a place × manner cell to reveal its symbol and an example word on a math-canvas chart grid, then flips into a scored quiz that asks for the manner of articulation of a shown symbol. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-ling-morphology.name: std-ling-morphology
std-ling-morphology.description: Morpheme tree builder — the learner attaches morphemes from a bank one at a time under order and category constraints (prefixes before the root, suffixes after, exactly one root), gets a validity verdict per attachment, and can check the built word against a gloss table; the growing word renders as a labelled tree on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-ling-phonology.name: std-ling-phonology
std-ling-phonology.description: Phoneme-vs-allophone classifier — the learner studies a dataset of sound pairs (minimal pairs or complementary distribution) and classifies the two sounds as separate phonemes or allophones of one phoneme, with the evidence rows, environments to consider, and distinctive-feature notes folded into the item prompt/hint and the distributional explanation revealed once picked. Composed as a domain binding of the std-learn-classify instrument atom — the dataset roster and the phonemes/allophones category ladder are config overrides on its items/categories knobs, with loopRound preserving the original's endless dataset cycle; the drill mechanics (pick, verdict, advance, score) come from std-learn-classify. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-ling-soundchange.name: std-ling-soundchange
std-ling-soundchange.description: Historical sound-change stepper — the learner applies ordered Great Vowel Shift rules one at a time and watches every word whose vowel matches strike all at once, rendering the before/after pronunciation on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-ling-syntaxtree.name: std-ling-syntaxtree
std-ling-syntaxtree.description: Universal Grammar syntax-tree builder — the learner assembles a sentence's constituent structure bottom-up, attaching one labelled bracket (NP, VP, PP, S) at a time in derivation order, with evidence text on every pick and a growing bracket-tree render on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-ling-vowels.name: std-ling-vowels
std-ling-vowels.description: Vowel formant explorer — F1/F2 stepper buttons move a point through the vowel quadrilateral on a math-canvas, the nearest cardinal vowel in the loaded inventory is identified by squared formant distance, and a rounding toggle switches between unrounded and rounded vowel sets. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-logic-fallacy.name: std-logic-fallacy
std-logic-fallacy.description: Fallacy classifier — an argument card is presented, the learner classifies it as valid or as a named fallacy (ad hominem, straw man, false dilemma, affirming the consequent), sees an immediate correct/incorrect verdict plus an explanation, and after the corpus reaches an end-of-round summary with a per-fallacy breakdown and a Retry affordance. Composed as a domain binding of the std-learn-classify generic classify-with-feedback instrument — the argument roster and fallacy-category vocabulary are config overrides on its items/categories knobs. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-logic-gates.name: std-logic-gates
std-logic-gates.description: Boolean circuit simulator — the learner toggles input pins, predicts the output bulb, then propagates values gate by gate (AND/OR/NOT/XOR) through the wired network (rendered as a layered algo-graph-canvas) to check the prediction. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (LogicGatesTransport); the circuit evaluation lives in the sibling LogicGatesSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (propagates the current circuit gate by gate — the same computation the tick used to run, and the same as the Propagate button), LEARN_RESET (reseeds the first circuit's inputs and clears any propagated values/prediction), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.LogicGatesTransport — one render authority per shared entity); Predict 1/0, Propagate, and Next Circuit remain as their own domain buttons for locking a prediction, a single manual evaluation, or advancing the circuit roster. Propagation is idempotent for unchanged inputs — done stays false always, there is no rest/completion condition to detect. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-logic-inference.name: std-logic-inference
std-logic-inference.description: Propositional inference engine — a domain binding of the std-learn-derivation goal-directed derivation atom, with modus ponens and modus tollens declared as its two candidate steps (Modus Ponens matches a fact against a link's left side and derives its right side; Modus Tollens matches a negated fact against a link's right side and derives the negated left side) over config-declared propositional premises. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-logic-quantifier.name: std-logic-quantifier
std-logic-quantifier.description: Predicate-logic model evaluator — a finite domain of objects with visible properties; the learner marks which ∀/∃ statements they believe true, evaluates them against the model, and can toggle object properties to flip a statement's truth. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-logic-truthtable.name: std-logic-truthtable
std-logic-truthtable.description: Propositional truth-table engine — the learner toggles atomic proposition P/Q/R truth values and watches compound formulas (AND/OR/NOT/IMPLIES) re-evaluate live against every row of the truth table. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-logic-venn.name: std-logic-venn
std-logic-venn.description: Syllogism Venn tester — the learner shades true lens regions (boolean circle-intersection fills, not centroid markers) and drops ✕ marks on a three-circle diagram for each premise of a categorical syllogism (All M are P, Some S are M), then tests whether the shaded diagram makes the conclusion valid. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-math-derivative.name: std-math-derivative
std-math-derivative.description: Slope viewer — a point rides a curve with its tangent line; an optional secant through x and x + h converges to the tangent as h shrinks, and the slope readout is f′(x). The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (MathDerivativeTransport); the point/function state and the h-halving convergence live in the sibling MathDerivativeSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (halves h toward hMin and recomputes the secant slope — the same computation the Halve h button runs), LEARN_RESET (reseeds the function preset, point, and h from config and clears done), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.MathDerivativeTransport — one render authority per shared entity); the function-preset buttons, x slider, and Show/Hide secant remain as their own domain affordances, and Halve h stays as its own distinct manual-step button running the identical computation LEARN_STEP runs. The sequence terminates: once h reaches hMin the subject sets done true (the subject is done's sole writer), which halts both the transport's auto-stepping clock and further manual Halve-h/Step presses. Composed as the derivative mode of the learning math lab. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-math-integral.name: std-math-integral
std-math-integral.description: Riemann-sum accumulator — each step doubles the rectangles under a curve, the left/right/midpoint/trapezoid rule is selectable, and the accumulated area converges to the exact integral readout. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (MathIntegralTransport); the rule selection, bounds, and rectangle-doubling accumulation live in the sibling MathIntegralSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (doubles the rectangle count toward maxRectangles and recomputes the Riemann sum — the same computation the Double rectangles button runs), LEARN_RESET (reseeds the function preset, rule, rectangle count, and bounds from config and clears done), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.MathIntegralTransport — one render authority per shared entity); the rule-picker buttons and lower/upper bound sliders remain as their own domain affordances, and Double rectangles stays as its own distinct manual-step button running the identical computation LEARN_STEP runs. The sequence terminates: once the rectangle count reaches maxRectangles the subject sets done true (the subject is done's sole writer), which halts both the transport's auto-stepping clock and further manual Double-rectangles/Step presses. Composed as the integral mode of the learning math lab. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-math-linear.name: std-math-linear
std-math-linear.description: Linear-systems lab instrument — line A pivots through a fixed point with a slope that increments one notch per Step (wrapping within a configured range), line B stays fixed and dashed; the intersection is recomputed and narrated every step, or narrated honestly as parallel when the slopes coincide. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (MathLinearTransport); the slope-stepping and intersection math live in the sibling MathLinearSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (advances slope A by one notch, wrapping within the configured range, and recomputes the intersection), LEARN_RESET (reseeds slope A and the lines from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.MathLinearTransport — one render authority per shared entity). The slope wraps within its configured range and never rests — done stays false always, there is no completion condition to detect. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-math-matrix.name: std-math-matrix
std-math-matrix.description: Linear-transform engine — 2×2 matrix entries (or rotation/scale/shear/reflection presets) morph a shape and the basis vectors live on the plane, with a determinant readout, cycling through presetCycle (identity, rotation, scale, shear, reflect by default). The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (MathMatrixTransport); the preset-cycling and matrix editing live in the sibling MathMatrixSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (advances to the next preset in the cycle and recomputes the transformed shape and basis vectors — the same computation the old preset-cycling tick used to run), LEARN_RESET (reseeds the matrix entries from config, clears the animation state, and returns to the first preset), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.MathMatrixTransport — one render authority per shared entity); the Identity/Rotate/Scale/Shear/Reflect preset buttons, per-entry sliders, and Show/Hide basis remain as their own domain affordances. The Animate button's 48ms interpolation runs through a domain tween clock (matrixAnimTick) that fires an internal ANIM_FRAME each frame — the ANIM_FRAME arm advances the interpolation and repaints with the transport strip embedded, since a ticks-context render cannot bind @trait directly. The preset cycle is indefinite, wrapping past the last entry in presetCycle back to the first — done stays false always, there is no rest/completion condition to detect. Composed as the matrix mode of the learning math lab. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-math-numberline.name: std-math-numberline
std-math-numberline.description: Integer number-line lab instrument — a marker hops signed stepSize increments along y=0 (wrapping within the configured range), with the live hop drawn as a MathHop arc from its old position to its new one. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (MathNumberlineTransport); the hop math lives in the sibling MathNumberlineSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (applies one signed hop, wrapping within the configured range), LEARN_RESET (reseeds the marker and line from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.MathNumberlineTransport — one render authority per shared entity). The marker wraps within its configured range and never rests — done stays false always, there is no completion condition to detect. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-math-quadratic.name: std-math-quadratic
std-math-quadratic.description: Parabola explorer — a/b/c sliders let the learner directly reshape y = ax² + bx + c between steps, while Next-preset/the transport clock cycle through three discriminant cases (two real roots, a repeated root, no real roots); the vertex, axis of symmetry, roots and discriminant readouts recompute on every change. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (MathQuadraticTransport); the coefficient math and preset-cycling live in the sibling MathQuadraticSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (advances to the next discriminant preset), LEARN_RESET (reseeds a/b/c from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.MathQuadraticTransport — one render authority per shared entity). The preset cycle wraps and never rests — done stays false always, there is no completion condition to detect. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-math-sequence.name: std-math-sequence
std-math-sequence.description: Sequence lab instrument — arithmetic (aₙ = a₀ + n·d) or geometric (aₙ = a₀·rⁿ) terms revealed one Step at a time against a dashed reference curve through every term; the just-revealed term is highlighted. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (MathSequenceTransport); the term-revealing math lives in the sibling MathSequenceSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (advances n by one term, recomputes the revealed points, and marks done once termCount terms are revealed), LEARN_RESET (reseeds n, the curve, and the revealed points from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.MathSequenceTransport — one render authority per shared entity). The sequence terminates: done becomes true once n reaches termCount − 1 (all termCount terms revealed), which halts the transport clock; Reset clears done and reseeds. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-math-sinewave.name: std-math-sinewave
std-math-sinewave.description: Sine wave lab instrument — y = A·sin(kx − φ) sampled fresh from amplitude/frequency/phase config on every step, plotted against a dashed un-shifted reference curve, phase advancing by π/8 each step. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (MathSineWaveTransport); the phase-advance sampling lives in the sibling MathSineWaveSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (advances phase by π/8 and resamples both curves), LEARN_RESET (reseeds phase to 0 and resamples from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.MathSineWaveTransport — one render authority per shared entity). The wave never terminates — done stays false always, there is no rest/completion condition to detect. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-math-unitcircle.name: std-math-unitcircle
std-math-unitcircle.description: Unit-circle lab instrument — a point sweeps a sampled circle while dashed cos/sin projection guides and a swept angle mark θ track it; readouts quote θ, cosθ, sinθ live. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (MathUnitCircleTransport); the angle-stepping and trig math live in the sibling MathUnitCircleSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (advances θ by π/12 and wraps continuously around the circle, recomputing cosθ/sinθ and the projection guides), LEARN_RESET (reseeds θ and the circle from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.MathUnitCircleTransport — one render authority per shared entity). θ wraps continuously around the circle and never rests — done stays false always, there is no completion condition to detect. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-math-vectors-3d.name: std-math-vectors-3d
std-math-vectors-3d.description: 3D vector-operations instrument — config-declared vectors u and v (x,y,z knobs) rendered as labeled arrows from the origin in a 3D scene via physics-canvas `vectors3d`, cycling four operation presets: u+v (both vectors plus the sum arrow and a tip-to-tail ghost of v shifted to u's tip), u·v (the scalar projection arrow of v onto u with the dot product and the angle θ between them read out), u×v (the cross product — the operation that only makes sense in 3D — drawn as the arrow perpendicular to both, with |u×v| read out as the parallelogram area), and s·u (scalar multiple); an optional unit-axis reference triad (labeled x/y/z arrows) orients the volume — the spatial geometry of vector algebra that a 2D canvas cannot show. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (Vectors3DTransport); the operation-cycling lives in the sibling Vectors3DSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (advances to the next operation preset — the same computation the tick used to run, and the same as the Step button), LEARN_RESET (reseeds u, v, scalar, and the operation index from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.Vectors3DTransport — one render authority per shared entity). The preset cycle is indefinite, wrapping past s·u back to u+v — done stays false always, there is no rest/completion condition to detect. Composed as the vectors-3d mode of the learning math lab. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-math-vectors.name: std-math-vectors
std-math-vectors.description: Vector addition lab instrument — vector A is fixed, vector B rotates by Δθ each step; a dashed ghost segment shows B placed tip-to-tail at A's tip, and the solid A+B resultant is drawn from the origin, narrated with the component sum every step. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (MathVectorsTransport); the vector rotation and resultant math live in the sibling MathVectorsSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (rotates B by Δθ and recomputes the resultant), LEARN_RESET (reseeds B and the resultant from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.MathVectorsTransport — one render authority per shared entity). B rotates by Δθ every step and never rests — done stays false always, there is no completion condition to detect. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-physics-circular.name: std-physics-circular
std-physics-circular.description: Circular-motion engine — integrates one body under a linear central force each substep and renders a physics-canvas with a center pivot, a radius-spoke rod, a sweeping angle marker, a centripetal vector, and a circular trail. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (CircularTransport); the orbital integration lives in the sibling CircularSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (applies one substepped central-force integration pass), LEARN_RESET (reseeds the pivot, spoke rod, trail, centripetal vector, angle, and readouts from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.CircularTransport — one render authority per shared entity). The orbit never terminates, so done stays false always. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-physics-collision.name: std-physics-collision
std-physics-collision.description: Elastic-collision engine — equal or per-body-mass circles exchange velocity along the collision normal and bounce off box walls, substepped for smooth motion; renders a physics-canvas with the wall box, per-body momentum vectors, an impact flash on colliding bodies, and total-momentum/kinetic-energy readouts.
