The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (CollisionTransport); the elastic-collision integration lives in the sibling CollisionSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (applies one substepped collision-and-bounce pass), LEARN_RESET (reseeds bodies, walls, vectors, and readouts from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.CollisionTransport — one render authority per shared entity). Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-physics-diagram.name: std-physics-diagram
std-physics-diagram.description: Generic declarative physics-diagram renderer — a fixed roster of labeled points and shapes (field lines, ray paths, or circuit wiring) drawn on a physics-canvas with no simulation tick; Step toggles body labels on/off and Reset restores them. Shape/point vocabulary is entirely config-declared, so the same mechanism serves any static physics sketch. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches — the same body serves the field/ray-diagram/circuit matchModes bound at each call site.

std-physics-field-3d.name: std-physics-field-3d
std-physics-field-3d.description: 3D electric-field instrument — samples the superposed Coulomb field E = Σ kq/r² · r̂ of a config-declared point-charge roster (a +/− dipole by default, with named presets stepped through in place) on a 3D grid of sample points around the charges and renders each sample as a labeled field-vector arrow through the volume via physics-canvas `vectors3d` — the field geometry between and around spatially separated charges that a 2D canvas cannot show; clicking a sample point reads out Ex/Ey/Ez/|E| numerically, and renders a 3D physics-canvas; composed as the field-3d mode of the learning physics lab. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-physics-freefall.name: std-physics-freefall
std-physics-freefall.description: Free-fall engine — bodies drop under gravity, substepped for smooth motion, bouncing off the ground and walls; renders a physics-canvas with a height ruler, per-ball trails, labeled gravity vectors, and per-ball velocity/height readouts. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (FreeFallTransport); the substepped integration lives in the sibling FreeFallSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (applies one substepped gravity/bounce integration pass and checks for ground/wall landings), LEARN_RESET (reseeds bodies, trails, vectors, landed markers, and readouts from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.FreeFallTransport — one render authority per shared entity). Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-physics-friction.name: std-physics-friction
std-physics-friction.description: Friction engine — decelerates sliding bodies via kinetic friction, substepped for smooth motion, and renders a physics-canvas with a hatched ground, opposing friction vectors, skid trails, and per-block speed readouts. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (FrictionTransport); the deceleration lives in the sibling FrictionSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (applies one substepped friction pass), LEARN_RESET (reseeds bodies, trails, vectors, and readouts from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.FrictionTransport — one render authority per shared entity). Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-physics-gas.name: std-physics-gas
std-physics-gas.description: Ideal-gas kinetic-theory engine — equal-mass particles bounce elastically off walls and each other in a box, substepped for smooth motion; particles are procedurally seeded from a count and mean speed, colored by their current speed band, and the physics-canvas shows the container walls plus particle-count/mean-speed/wall-hit readouts. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (GasTransport); the collision integration lives in the sibling GasSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (applies one substepped elastic-collision pass across walls and particles), LEARN_RESET (reseeds particles, walls, and readouts from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.GasTransport — one render authority per shared entity). The gas simulation never reaches a terminal state — done stays false for the life of the orbital. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-physics-incline.name: std-physics-incline
std-physics-incline.description: Inclined-plane engine — slides a block down a frictional ramp under gravity via line-projection, substepped for smooth motion, and renders a physics-canvas with the ramp, an angle marker at its base, and three labeled vectors (gravity, normal, friction) computed from the ramp slope. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (InclineTransport); the ramp slide lives in the sibling InclineSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (applies one substepped ramp-projection pass), LEARN_RESET (reseeds the ramp, block, vectors, and readouts from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.InclineTransport — one render authority per shared entity). Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-physics-magnetic.name: std-physics-magnetic
std-physics-magnetic.description: Magnetic cyclotron engine — charged bodies integrate under F=qv×B inside a into-page field region, substepped for smooth motion, and render a physics-canvas with capped cyclotron trails, a labeled force vector perpendicular to velocity, and a gyroradius readout. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (MagneticTransport); the cyclotron force integration lives in the sibling MagneticSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (applies one substepped force pass), LEARN_RESET (reseeds bodies, trails, vectors, and readouts from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.MagneticTransport — one render authority per shared entity). A cyclotron orbit never naturally terminates, so done stays false-only here — this atom has no completion condition. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-physics-orbit-3d.name: std-physics-orbit-3d
std-physics-orbit-3d.description: 3D orbital-mechanics instrument — integrates up to three bodies under softened inverse-square gravity about a fixed emissive central star in scene cells every tick, demonstrating orbital inclination and node geometry (equatorial, 45°, and polar planes) that a 2D canvas cannot show, and renders a 3D physics-canvas with per-body trajectory trails via `uses`; composed as the orbit-3d mode of the learning physics lab. The Run/Pause/Reset/speed transport and the sim clock come from the std-learn-sim-3d atom (Orbit3DSim); the gravity physics lives in the sibling Orbit3DPhysics trait, which transitions directly on the transport's SIM_3D_TICK (integrates the bodies from ?dt) and SIM_3D_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport shell is embedded via @trait.Orbit3DSim — one render authority per shared entity). Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-physics-orbit.name: std-physics-orbit
std-physics-orbit.description: Orbital-motion engine — planets integrate under inverse-square gravity toward a fixed central mass, substepped for smooth motion, and render a physics-canvas with self-tracing capped orbit trails, a labeled velocity vector per planet, and radius/speed readouts. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (OrbitTransport); the gravity integration lives in the sibling OrbitSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (applies one substepped gravity integration pass), LEARN_RESET (reseeds bodies, trails, vectors, and readouts from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.OrbitTransport — one render authority per shared entity). The orbit never terminates — done stays false throughout. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-physics-pendulum.name: std-physics-pendulum
std-physics-pendulum.description: Pendulum engine — swings a bob about a fixed pivot via rigid-length projection, substepped for smooth motion, and renders a physics-canvas with a pivot fixture, a rod, an angle marker measured from vertical, a bob trail, and labeled tension/gravity vectors. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (PendulumTransport); the swing lives in the sibling PendulumSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (applies one substepped rigid-length projection pass), LEARN_RESET (reseeds bodies, trails, vectors, angles, and readouts from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.PendulumTransport — one render authority per shared entity); a pendulum never reaches rest in this model, so done stays false-only. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-physics-projectile-3d.name: std-physics-projectile-3d
std-physics-projectile-3d.description: 3D projectile-motion instrument — launches a ball from a ground pad with configurable speed, elevation, and azimuth and integrates it under gravity in scene cells every tick (z is height), demonstrating the out-of-plane launch direction a 2D canvas cannot show, tracking apex height, range, and flight time against an optional analytic target marker and a capped apex-to-impact trail, rendered through a 3D physics-canvas; composed as the projectile-3d mode of the learning physics lab. The Run/Pause/Reset/speed transport and the sim clock come from the std-learn-sim-3d atom (Projectile3DSim); the launch seeding, gravity integration, landing/apex/range/flight-time tracking, and the full-shell scene render live in the sibling Projectile3DPhysics trait, which transitions directly on the transport's SIM_3D_TICK (integrates the ball from ?dt) and SIM_3D_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and pauses the transport with an emitted PAUSE the instant the ball lands (the transport shell is embedded via @trait.Projectile3DSim — one render authority per shared entity). Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-physics-projectile.name: std-physics-projectile
std-physics-projectile.description: Projectile-motion engine — integrates bodies under constant gravity with wall/ground bounce, substepped for smooth motion, and renders a physics-canvas with trails, a labeled velocity vector, and height/range/speed readouts. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (ProjectileTransport); the gravity/bounce integration lives in the sibling ProjectileSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (applies one substepped integration batch), LEARN_RESET (reseeds bodies, trails, vectors, and readouts from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.ProjectileTransport — one render authority per shared entity). Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-physics-reflection.name: std-physics-reflection
std-physics-reflection.description: Reflection engine — photons travel in straight lines and bounce off mirror wall/ground segments, substepped for smooth motion; renders a physics-canvas with capped photon trails and a paired angle-of-incidence/angle-of-reflection marker at the most recent bounce. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (ReflectionTransport); the bounce physics lives in the sibling ReflectionSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (applies one substepped photon-bounce pass), LEARN_RESET (reseeds bodies, trails, and the bounce markers from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.ReflectionTransport — one render authority per shared entity). Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-physics-spring.name: std-physics-spring
std-physics-spring.description: Spring engine — a mass on a Hooke's-law spring pulled toward an anchor point, substepped for smooth motion, and renders a physics-canvas with a wall fixture, a dashed equilibrium guide, and a labeled restoring-force vector. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (SpringTransport); the Hooke's-law integration lives in the sibling SpringSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (applies one substepped spring integration pass), LEARN_RESET (reseeds the mass, trail, vector, and readouts from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.SpringTransport — one render authority per shared entity). A spring oscillator never settles: `done` is written false-only (by INIT/MODE_SELECTED/LEARN_RESET) and never set true, so LEARN_STEP's guard keeps admitting steps indefinitely. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-physics-wave-3d.name: std-physics-wave-3d
std-physics-wave-3d.description: 3D surface wave / ripple tank — a gridSize×gridSize height-field surface whose height (scene z) follows a superposition of traveling waves z = Σ A·sin(k·r − ωt) radiating from one or two config-declared sources, demonstrating circular wavefronts, straight plane waves, and the two-source interference pattern that a 2D canvas cannot show, rendered as a physics-canvas `surface3d` mesh with the source markers as bodies. Composed as the wave-3d mode of the learning physics lab. The Run/Pause/Reset/speed transport and the sim clock come from the std-learn-sim-3d atom (Wave3DSim); the wave physics lives in the sibling Wave3DPhysics trait, which transitions directly on the transport's SIM_3D_TICK (drives the wave phase from ?dt/?simTime) and SIM_3D_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport shell is embedded via @trait.Wave3DSim — one render authority per shared entity). Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-physics-wave.name: std-physics-wave
std-physics-wave.description: Wave engine — a chain of coupled oscillators where each interior point accelerates toward its neighbors' average height, propagating an initial pulse; renders a physics-canvas with a dashed equilibrium line, displacement-colored points, and an oscilloscope trace of the first moving point's displacement over time. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (WaveTransport); the wave propagation lives in the sibling WaveSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (applies one substepped coupled-oscillator pass), LEARN_RESET (reseeds shapes, bodies, traces, and readouts from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.WaveTransport — one render authority per shared entity). Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-prob-bayes.name: std-prob-bayes
std-prob-bayes.description: Interactive Bayes' theorem engine — priors/likelihoods sliders drive a population split (true/false positive/negative counts) and a computed posterior via Bayes' rule, rendered as world-coordinate bar charts on a math-canvas, with a live meter comparing the analytic posterior to an empirical one built up trial by trial. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (ProbBayesTransport); the trial-drawing lives in the sibling ProbBayesSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (draws a random individual and folds the result into the empirical posterior — the same computation Run Evidence Trial performs manually), LEARN_RESET (clears the trial history and empirical posterior), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.ProbBayesTransport — one render authority per shared entity); Run Evidence Trial remains as its own domain button for a single manual draw. Trials accumulate without limit — done stays false always, there is no rest/completion condition to detect (the narration calls out analytic/empirical convergence but never halts the trial clock). Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-prob-binomial.name: std-prob-binomial
std-prob-binomial.description: Binomial trial accumulator — each run flips n coins with bias p and drops the head-count into a world-coordinate histogram (count axis) that converges to the theoretical binomial PMF overlaid as expected-count markers, on a math-canvas. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (ProbBinomialTransport); the trial-running lives in the sibling ProbBinomialSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (runs one trial — flips n coins and folds the head-count into the histogram, the same computation the tick used to run, and the same as Run Trial), LEARN_RESET (clears the accumulated counts and histogram), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.ProbBinomialTransport — one render authority per shared entity); Run Trial and Run Many remain as their own domain buttons for a single manual trial or a batch of runsPerStep trials. Runs accumulate until maxRuns is reached, at which point done becomes true and the sim halts (the transport clock's own guard also checks done, so it stops firing LEARN_STEP) until Reset clears it. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-prob-clt.name: std-prob-clt
std-prob-clt.description: Central Limit Theorem engine — pick a population shape (uniform, skewed, bimodal); each draw takes a sample of size n and drops the sample mean into a growing means-histogram, rendered in world coordinates with a true-mean guide line, that visibly narrows and normalizes as draws accumulate, on a math-canvas. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (ProbCltTransport); the sampling lives in the sibling ProbCltSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (draws one sample and folds its mean into the histogram — the same computation the tick used to run, and the same as Draw Sample), LEARN_RESET (clears the accumulated means and histogram), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.ProbCltTransport — one render authority per shared entity); Draw Sample and Draw Many remain as their own domain buttons for a single manual draw or a batch of drawsPerStep draws. Draws accumulate without limit — done stays false always, there is no rest/completion condition to detect. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-prob-confidence.name: std-prob-confidence
std-prob-confidence.description: Confidence-interval capture engine — each draw samples n values, builds a confidence interval for the mean, and stacks it as a world-coordinate row; intervals missing the true mean turn red while the running capture rate converges to the nominal confidence level, on a math-canvas. The Draw Interval/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (ProbConfidenceTransport); the interval-drawing lives in the sibling ProbConfidenceSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (draws one interval — samples n values and stacks a confidence interval row, the same computation the tick used to run, and the same as Draw Interval), LEARN_RESET (clears the accumulated intervals and rows), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.ProbConfidenceTransport — one render authority per shared entity); Draw Interval and Draw Many remain as their own domain buttons for a single manual draw or a batch of intervalsPerStep draws. Draws accumulate until maxRows is reached, at which point done becomes true and the sim halts (the transport clock's own guard also checks done, so it stops firing LEARN_STEP) until Reset clears it. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-prob-galton.name: std-prob-galton
std-prob-galton.description: Galton board engine — balls fall under gravity and random-walk past pegs on a physics-canvas board; each ball that reaches the floor is counted into a bin by x-position and respawned from the top, and a second math-canvas below turns the accumulating bin counts into a live histogram — the bell curve, finally quantified. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (GaltonTransport); the physics stepping lives in the sibling GaltonSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (applies one substepped gravity+jitter pass, counting landed balls into bins and respawning them), LEARN_RESET (reseeds the pegs, walls, balls, bins, and readouts from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.GaltonTransport — one render authority per shared entity). Balls respawn immediately on landing so the board runs forever — done stays false always, there is no rest/completion condition to detect. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-prob-montecarlo.name: std-prob-montecarlo
std-prob-montecarlo.description: Monte-Carlo π engine — each Step draws a batch of uniform points in the unit square on a math-canvas, colors them by whether they land inside the quarter circle, and accumulates them (capped) against a sampled quarter-circle arc; the running inside-fraction × 4 estimates π, with honest convergence narration. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (MonteCarloTransport); the sampling lives in the sibling MonteCarloSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (draws one batch of points, updates the capped point cloud, running counts, and π estimate), LEARN_RESET (reseeds the point cloud, counters, and readouts from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.MonteCarloTransport — one render authority per shared entity). Sampling never halts on its own — the point cloud is capped for rendering but n/insideCount/π estimate keep accumulating uncapped — so done stays false always, there is no rest/completion condition to detect. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-prob-normal-distribution.name: std-prob-normal-distribution
std-prob-normal-distribution.description: Bell-curve explorer — mean and standard-deviation sliders let the learner directly reshape the Gaussian curve between steps, while Step/the transport clock cycle through three named presets (standard/wide/shifted) that jump the mean and spread; the peak height and 68% ±1σ band redraw on every change. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (NormalDistributionTransport); the curve math and preset-cycling live in the sibling NormalDistributionSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (advances to the next preset — a mean/standard-deviation pair, the same computation the tick used to run), LEARN_RESET (reseeds mean, standard deviation and the preset index from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.NormalDistributionTransport — one render authority per shared entity). The preset cycle wraps and never rests — done stays false always, there is no completion condition to detect. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-prob-regression.name: std-prob-regression
std-prob-regression.description: Least-squares explorer composing std-learn-scatter-fit — the regression-lesson realization of the generic scatter-fit instrument: a seed scatter dataset, the least-squares fit line, dashed residual segments, live r/R², and guess-the-line scoring, on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-prob-trials.name: std-prob-trials
std-prob-trials.description: Trials simulator — draws one outcome from a weighted sample space (default: a fair six-sided die; reconfigure outcomes for a coin flip, a weighted spinner, or any categorical distribution) and accumulates it into an observed-count histogram overlaid with expected-count markers on a math-canvas. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (ProbTrialsTransport); the sampling lives in the sibling ProbTrialsSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (draws one outcome and folds it into the observed-count histogram — the same computation the tick used to run, and the same as Roll), LEARN_RESET (clears the accumulated counts and histogram back to zero), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.ProbTrialsTransport — one render authority per shared entity); Roll remains as its own domain button for a single manual trial. Trials accumulate without limit — done stays false always, there is no rest/completion condition to detect. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-prob-walk.name: std-prob-walk
std-prob-walk.description: Random-walk engine — a cloud of walkers starts at the origin and random-steps each tick into a widening Gaussian on a math-canvas, with a second math-canvas below quantifying the spread as a live displacement histogram bucketed by x-position. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (WalkTransport); the random-walk stepping lives in the sibling WalkSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (applies one substepped random displacement pass to every walker and rebuckets the displacement histogram), LEARN_RESET (reseeds the walker cloud, histogram, and readouts from config), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.WalkTransport — one render authority per shared entity). Walkers diffuse without bound and never settle, so there is no rest/completion condition to detect — done stays false always. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-psych-conditioning.name: std-psych-conditioning
std-psych-conditioning.description: Classical (Pavlovian) conditioning trial-runner — the learner runs CS+US pairing trials to drive an associative-strength curve toward its asymptote (acquisition), or runs CS-alone trials to drive it toward zero (extinction), via the Rescorla-Wagner rule plotted on a biology-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-psych-memory.name: std-psych-memory
std-psych-memory.description: Memory-retention engine — the Ebbinghaus forgetting curve: retention decays exponentially with time since the last repetition, ADD_REPETITION recovers a fraction of the forgotten gap (full boost under the spaced preset, half under massed, so the learner can compare the two schedules), and a no-repetition reference decay is plotted alongside on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-psych-operant.name: std-psych-operant
std-psych-operant.description: Operant-conditioning engine — FR/VR/FI/VI reinforcement schedules drive a cumulative-response curve: ratio schedules make a reinforcer available after a fixed (or alternating variable) number of responses, interval schedules after a fixed (or alternating variable) amount of time, and each delivered reinforcer inserts a post-reinforcement pause that draws the characteristic scallop on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-psych-signal.name: std-psych-signal
std-psych-signal.description: Signal-detection-theory engine — noise and signal+noise evidence distributions (unit-variance Gaussians separated by dPrime) are plotted on a math-canvas; the learner drags the decision criterion and the theoretical hit rate Φ(d′ − c) and false-alarm rate Φ(−c) recompute (the ROC point), and RUN_TRIALS samples empirical hits and false alarms at the configured base rate. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-psych-stroop.name: std-psych-stroop
std-psych-stroop.description: Stroop-task engine — the learner names the ink color of each displayed word while the word itself names a (matching or conflicting) color; congruent and incongruent trials are scored separately and the interference aggregate (congruent accuracy − incongruent accuracy) is tracked, with the stimulus rendered as a text shape on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-soc-conformity.name: std-soc-conformity
std-soc-conformity.description: Conformity engine — agents on a grid adopt the local majority opinion of their row-ordered neighborhood each step, except a deviance-rate share who deliberately break with it, so the population converges or fragments over repeated steps, on a biology-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-soc-deviance.name: std-soc-deviance
std-soc-deviance.description: Deviance & labeling engine — the learner classifies each act through labeling theory: conforming, primary deviance (norm violation, informal sanction), or secondary deviance (formal label applied and internalized), with per-item feedback and an explanation revealed once picked. Composed as a domain binding of the std-learn-classify instrument atom — the scenario roster and category ladder are config overrides on its items/categories knobs; the drill mechanics (pick, verdict, advance, round summary, retry) come from std-learn-classify. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-soc-imagination.name: std-soc-imagination
std-soc-imagination.description: Sociological Imagination engine — C. Wright Mills' exercise linking a personal trouble to the structural public issue behind it, with a drawn trouble→issue node map, per-link feedback and a running score, on a biology-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-soc-mobility.name: std-soc-mobility
std-soc-mobility.description: Intergenerational mobility engine — a 5x5 quintile transition matrix whose rows (parent's quintile) the learner edits cell by cell; each edit renormalizes the row and recomputes the immobility, upward-mobility, and rags-to-riches rates, with a perfect-mobility benchmark overlay, on a biology-canvas heat grid. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-soc-network.name: std-soc-network
std-soc-network.description: Small-world network engine — a ring graph whose edges the learner rewires on and off: degree centrality is recomputed live, weak-tie bridges are highlighted, and a complex-contagion diffusion step spreads adoption through one strong tie or a pair of weak ties, on a biology-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-soc-stratification.name: std-soc-stratification
std-soc-stratification.description: Social stratification & mobility engine — five class strata redistribute across generations as the learner drives an intergenerational mobility index, with a live Gini-index readout, on a biology-canvas stacked bar. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

mesh-asset-catalog.name: mesh-asset-catalog
mesh-asset-catalog.description: MeshAssetCatalog — headless publisher that makes any mesh asset organism canvas-ready: INIT emits MESH_ASSET_PUBLISH { kind, states } where states maps anim state name (idle/walk/attack/hit/death/...) to draw-group items of draw-mesh descriptors authored in cell coordinates (z = height), each layer carrying its own keyframe animation — all pure config. mesh-material-crystal.name: mesh-material-crystal
mesh-material-crystal.description: MeshMaterialCrystal — the 3D style contract's CRYSTAL recipe as a composable molecule: one draw-group applying the crystal rendering of the active style direction to any config shape. Where the 2D twin branches gradient+sparkle layers, this branches draw-mesh MATERIALS on the SAME geometry+palette: glossy (physical glass — transmission 0.8, ior 1.5, roughness 0.1 — the default, needs the rig's room environment to read as glass), flat (unlit basic fill), cartoon (toon bands + inverted-hull contour outline), neon (dark body driven by an emissive highlight with a default intensity pulse — pair with the neon rig's bloom), low-poly (glossy's transmission PBR with flatShading + the lowSegments tessellation — in 3D low-poly IS a token, standing in for the 2D twin's cutout/noir directions which don't apply to a volumetric mesh). Call sites override geometry + palette steps + style only; the recipes themselves are the molecule. Defaults derive from mesh-palette's style contract (arcane palette, materials.crystal preset).

mesh-material-magic.name: mesh-material-magic
mesh-material-magic.description: MeshMaterialMagic — the 3D style contract's MAGIC recipe as a composable molecule: one draw-group applying the magical-energy rendering of the active style direction to any config shape. Where the 2D twin branches gradient+halo layers, this branches draw-mesh MATERIALS on the SAME geometry+palette: glossy (emissive-driven standard PBR core with a gentle idle bob+pulse — the default), flat (unlit fill, static — no default pulse), cartoon (toon bands + inverted-hull contour outline, static), neon (dark body driven by a brighter emissive highlight with the default bob+pulse — pair with the neon rig's bloom), low-poly (glossy's emissive PBR with flatShading + the lowSegments tessellation, still bobbing+pulsing — in 3D low-poly IS a token, standing in for the 2D twin's cutout/noir directions which don't apply to a volumetric mesh). Call sites override geometry + palette steps + style only; the recipes themselves are the molecule. Defaults derive from mesh-palette's style contract (arcane palette, materials.magic preset, motion.idleMs bob+pulse).

mesh-material-metal.name: mesh-material-metal
mesh-material-metal.description: MeshMaterialMetal — the 3D style contract's METAL recipe as a composable molecule: one draw-group applying the metal rendering of the active style direction to any config shape. Where the 2D twin branches gradient layers, this branches draw-mesh MATERIALS on the SAME geometry+palette: glossy (standard PBR, metalness 0.9 roughness 0.25 — chrome under the room environment, the default), flat (unlit basic fill), cartoon (toon bands + inverted-hull contour outline), neon (dark body driven by an emissive highlight with a default intensity pulse — pair with the neon rig's bloom), low-poly (glossy's PBR with flatShading + the lowSegments tessellation — in 3D low-poly IS a token). Call sites override geometry + palette steps + style only; the recipes themselves are the molecule. Defaults derive from mesh-palette's style contract (iron palette, materials.metal preset).

mesh-palette.name: mesh-palette
mesh-palette.description: MeshPalette — the 3D STYLE CONTRACT atom: the library's volumetric art bible as declared data. Owns @entity.meshPalettes (named 5-step color value scales — the same color language as SvgPalette) and @entity.meshStyle (style direction token, per-style lighting rig, PBR material recipes, post-process presets, proportion grid, shape language, motion timing) — every 3D style variable the mesh asset corpus follows, overridable per game via config. The style token names the theme direction (glossy | flat | cartoon | neon | low-poly) every material/mesh molecule branches its recipe on — one flip restyles all material-composed meshes. Seed-only atom (no render trait); compose alongside MeshPrimitiveRender (base geometry) and any material/outline molecules built on top.

mesh-part-gear.name: mesh-part-gear
mesh-part-gear.description: MeshPartGear — the 3D twin of svg-part-gear: the equipment kit as one draw-group at the character root (config position) — leather belt box with a gold front buckle at hip height, right-thigh holster box, and a back-left belt pouch. All hip-band gear rides the ROOT (not the leg bones), so it stays put while limbs swing. Style flips MATERIALS on the shared geometry (glossy PBR default, flat, cartoon toon+outline, neon emissive, low-poly flat-shaded); metals collapse to dark keepers only in the neon branch where everything glows.

mesh-part-head-banded.name: mesh-part-head-banded
mesh-part-head-banded.description: MeshPartHeadBanded — the 3D twin of svg-part-head-banded on the VRM head bone: a draw-group at the NECK joint (config position) whose items are authored neck-local — skull sphere, olive brow band cylinder, back knot box with two fluttering tail boxes, and two eye slits on the +y face side. In 3D the facing axis vanishes: the same head serves every yaw, so there is no per-facing geometry chain — style flips MATERIALS only (glossy PBR default, flat unlit, cartoon toon+outline, neon emissive, low-poly flat-shaded). The `nod` animation swings the whole head bone; `tailAnimation` flutters the band tails independently (a second animation cannot stack on the bone bob — same rule as the 2D part).

mesh-part-limb.name: mesh-part-limb
mesh-part-limb.description: MeshPartLimb — the 3D two-bone limb (VRM upperArm>lowerArm / upperLeg>lowerLeg): ONE molecule serves all four limbs. The root draw-group sits at the shoulder/hip JOINT (config position) and swings via the `swing` animation; a nested draw-group at the elbow/knee carries the lower segment and swings via `lowerSwing` — children are authored joint-local, so the chain articulates like a skeleton bone chain (rotate the shoulder and the forearm follows). Geometry is parametric config (capsule lengths/radii, joint sphere, hand/foot end), so unlike the 2D svg limb no per-facing re-authoring exists at all — facing is the consumer's yaw. Style flips MATERIALS only on the shared geometry: glossy PBR (default), flat unlit, cartoon toon+outline, neon emissive on a dark base, low-poly flat-shaded at lowSegments. Sign conventions (three right-hand Euler, scene y = world Z): hanging segments swing forward (scene +y) with NEGATIVE rotateX; knee flex is positive, elbow flex negative.

mesh-part-torso-suit.name: mesh-part-torso-suit

Style flips MATERIALS on the shared geometry (glossy PBR default, flat, cartoon toon+outline, neon emissive, low-poly flat-shaded). The `breathe` animation moves the whole torso bone; forward lean is POSITIVE rotateX (above-pivot mass, opposite sign from hanging limbs).

mesh-part-unit-base.name: mesh-part-unit-base

riya-game-platformer-open-world.name: riya-game-platformer-open-world
riya-game-platformer-open-world.description: riya open world · The Open Line — all twenty-four riya worlds stitched into ONE continuous 618-unit map you run left-to-right with a follow camera: the math window recenters on riya every frame (clamped to the world edges, with a small lead toward her facing), so the whole curriculum — number line → functions → limits → calculus → series → multivar — is one unbroken run. Skating is global: every skate world's curve is concatenated into one strictly-increasing mega-curve for std-platformer-body, densely resampled (monotone cubic, kinks preserved) so the ride and the drawing are the same smooth surface. GAME ELEMENTS: ✖ patrol bugs pace beats in six zones (std-patrol-hazard) and cost a life on touch; three glowing star doors (std-gate-lock) open at 20/50/80 ★; a treasure ring floats above the Gallery bars — loop one full revolution around the floating chest (std-loop-lock tracks your winding angle: θ = 2π opens it) and it spills 5 bonus 💎★; two velocity gates (std-velocity-gate) guard bonus gems off the through-path — cross the Deriv ramp gate inside its speed band (your speed IS the derivative) and hold still at the Mountain summit (slope 0) until the dwell opens it; twelve floor pads (std-pad-lock) form one world-wide checklist — mirrored pairs on the Valley and Shifts parabolas (lighting one side demands its mirror), one pad on each Corner wall, and two ordered rows on the Volume slabs where the inner sum's row must finish before the outer's (Σ); the ground itself teaches too: Doubling's floating steps double their gaps until one beats any jump (take the spring), the Series steps converge under a bonus cluster that hovers at the limit, Decay's landing pads shrink ×0.7 each, the Pole's asymptote gets a star trail up the void, and Log's domain simply has no floor left of x = −7 — jump the gap; four area fills (std-area-fill) turn motion into painted integrals — shade the Area run's region by pacing it, climb the Accum gauge fastest on the bump's high shelf, finish the Tail's finite area long before its infinite run ends, and keep the Taylor ride-band alive only while truly skating the wave; drift fields push riya like weather — cubic's inflection tugs from both sides, the vector step is a constant right-up current, gradient's arrows are the easy path uphill, the saddle's downdraft slams every jump over the pass (the max shoves you back down to the trail), and the contour patrol bobs on a sine; checkpoints at every zone entry (std-lives) are the respawn — three lives, then game over → retry. MATH YOU FEEL: while skating, std-learn-slope-probe draws the live tangent line, a rise-over-run triangle, and a glowing curve window under riya, with a dy/dx chip in the HUD; std-fx-trail leaves a comet trail. A GIF tutorial modal (std-tutorial-overlay) teaches run/jump, skating, and stars-doors on first boot (help button re-opens). Catch every ★ the line offers — stars and spilled gems alike — to clear it. Rendered through math-canvas on theme-token grid/axes with per-family zone bands.

riya-game-platformer.name: riya-game-platformer
riya-game-platformer.description: riya the dot escapes the rail. In riya-game she was a bead slid ALONG the graphs; here the graphs are the landscape and she runs and jumps across them on foot. Twenty-eight worlds, one per math idea, all composed from the std game substrate — platformer-body (run/jump physics, one-way AABB terrain collision, pit-fall signal, curve-skating) + objective-flow (win gate) + fx-particles — rendered through math-canvas so the axes, the numbers, and the world's own function curve stay visible at all times. The arc: 1) The Plain — the number line as flat ground with pits; x is a number you stand on. 2) The Ramp — a staircase rising 1 per 2 across; slope is how fast you climb. 3) The Valley — y = x²/16 sampled into bars; you drop into the parabola and jump back up its walls. 4) The Mountain — a climb to the one summit star: the local maximum, where the slope flattens to zero. 5) The Pole — the ground rises toward a chasm at x = 3 that swallows you: the asymptote, the x the world never touches. 6) The Doubling Stair — steps of 1, 2, 4, 8: each costs double, and the last wall is too tall for your legs unless you find the springboard. 7) The Gallery — a Riemann skyline: the bars ARE the function, and you walk across its area. 8) Shifts — the same valley moved right 4: (x−4) transforms the function. 9) Corner — y = |x|/2: the slope jumps from −½ to +½ at a point with no slope. 10) Inflection — x³: steep, flat, steep; the slope's slope flips sign. 11) Log — ln(x+7): a burst that flattens forever, forbidden left of x = −7. 12) Derivative — the ramp you skate IS world 3's slope, drawn beside its ghost. 13) Area — the shaded region piles up behind you as you run: integration. 14) Accumulation — a hill whose height collects a dashed bump. 15) Decay — exponential decay toward a floor you never touch (y′ = −ky). 16) Tail — 1 + 12/(x+12): an infinite tail whose area stays finite (improper integral). 17) Series — steps 1, ½, ¼, … that never cross the ceiling 2 (geometric series). 18) Taylor — a line and a cubic hugging the sine wave you skate. 19) Vectors — every tread is the same displacement ⟨1.6, 1⟩; walking adds vectors tip-to-tail. 20) Contours — the skyline is a slice of the hill z = 7 − x²/16, with level lines z = 2, 4, 6 behind it. 21) Partials — the plane z = 3 + x/4 + y/2 slopes ¼ under your feet and ½ in the dashed direction. 22) Gradient — purple ∇f arrows always aim at the summit of the gaussian hill. 23) Saddle — the pass is the trail's minimum and the cross-trail's maximum at once. 24) Volume — each column is one sum; the climb across is the second sum: ∬ f dA. Every world: catch every ★ to clear; fall in a pit and riya climbs back at her spawn with every star kept — no punishment, this is a beginner's mountain Each world is its own atom under riya/atoms (riya-level-*) owning its entity contract, knobs, and page; this organism only rebinds them.

riya-game.name: riya-game
riya-game.description: Riya — a math journey GAME with real physics, structured as an app: a collection of orbitals, one per world, plus a menu. Riya is a dot, a point in space with MASS: the player pushes it with arrows / WASD (hold to accelerate — keyMap/keyUpMap on the math-canvas) or taps the d-pad (velocity impulses), and the std-motion-body authority integrates gravity, acceleration, speed, damping, and walls every 50ms. Seven worlds climb the math ladder: the number line (/riya-line — coast and brake onto the ★ numbers), functions (/riya-curve — riya rides y = 0.25x² − 4, the rule picks your height), the derivative (/riya-slope — the hill's slope pushes back through motion-body's bias field; park where slope = 0), the turning points (/riya-peak — a cubic's hilltop and valley, both flat spots of f(x) = 0.5x³ − 1.5x), the limit (/riya-limit — ride f(x) = 8/x toward the wall at x = 0 and watch the f(x) chip explode), the exponential (/riya-expo — the doubling curve 2^(x/2) − 1, flat then a rocket), and the integral (/riya-area — walk the strip, paint every column, watch area = … add up). Numbers are always on screen: tick labels on every axis and live HUD chips (x, v, f(x), slope, area) next to the ★ score, a velocity arrow on riya, and the tangent line under it on the slope world. EVENT HYGIENE (learned the hard way): the client runtime drains its actor queue in FIFO, so a per-tick event subscription floods it and everything lags — this game therefore keeps ticks SET-ONLY (motion integrates; the play trait's gameTick collects stars / paints strips / writes the hill bias directly onto the shared entity) and reserves events for sparse, meaningful occurrences: keydown/keyup thrust, d-pad impulses, a star collected (BURST + PROGRESS), the gate's GAME_END. Each world composes std-motion-body + std-objective-flow + std-fx-particles with events renamed per world; collection runs in the play trait's gameTick because std-objective-reach's contract is discrete HERO_STEPPED steps, not continuous motion (see Almadar_Std_Game_Gaps.md). RiyaMenuOrbital (/riya) is the shell: title plus a button per world that (navigate ...)s into it. Clearing a world pops its clear overlay; Next ▶ navigates to the next world's page — and the final world's overlay is the RIYA COMPLETE celebration, returning to the menu. CONFLICT LAYER (v5.1): every good game needs an obstacle, and in riya the obstacle is the math itself — the misconception made physical. The LIMIT world's pole is a hazard: cross the danger line at x = 0.85 and the asymptote flings riya back and takes the last collected ★ (inDanger edge-guard so one entry = one penalty). The DOUBLING world has an antagonist: a second motion-body (the ghost, labeled 2^n) steered by the gameTick toward riya with acceleration ghostThrust·2^(stars held) — every ★ you carry doubles its hunger; a catch costs the last ★ and teleports the ghost back to its spawn (ghostArmed re-arm hysteresis at rearmDistance 2 prevents chain-drains). The AREA world's final ★ is a concept gate: gray and uncollectible until all 16 strips are painted — you cannot finish before the whole sum is laid down. (Pages are mount-scoped in the playground runtime, so cross-page run state like a persistent star bank would need a persistence-backed entity — out of scope; each world's HUD tracks its own ★ score.)
